summary: Kodo Kawamura (1933–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his master's and doctorate degrees at Komazawa University, where he also served as a professor from circa 1962 to 2004.
Kodo Nomura (1882–1963) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and later held a researcher post at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Koho Sawada, Zenko Sawada, Sotan Oka, Ryo-un Fueoka, and Join Saeki, and held posts as professor at Komazawa University and abbot of Antai-ji.
Kodo Yamada (1866–1933) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Komazawa University under Shiro Matsumoto and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.
Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst (born 1959) is a scholar in Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed an MA at KU Leuven (~1979–1999) and studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1992).

Kogen Mizuno (1901–2006) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a Doctorate of Letters from the University of Tokyo, served as a professor there (1959–1962), and was a professor and president at Komazawa University.
Koichi Hiraoka (born 1961) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and is attested as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University in 2026.

Koichi Hokazono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn, earned a PhD at Kyushu University, and held posts at Kyushu University and Kagoshima International University.

Koichi Shinohara (born 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Senior Lecturer in Religious Studies at Yale University from circa 2004.

Koichi Takahashi (born 1973) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito, subsequently holding assistant, project researcher, and professor posts there.

Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and under Gyōin Hashimoto, and served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1973–2006).
Koin Takada (1924–1998) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1941–1947). He was a disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto, whom he succeeded in 1967.

Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara and held posts at Kyoto Sangyo University and the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Koji Shindo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has been a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies and held a part-time lecturer post at Aichi Gakuin University in 2015.

Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University and Bukkyo University, where he earned a doctorate and served as assistant professor (~1968–2004) and professor (~1976–2004).
Koji Tanaka is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Macquarie University, the University of Auckland, and the Australian National University.

Kojiro Yoshikawa (1904–1980) was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and president of Toho Gakkai (~1973–1980).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Waseda University under Sokichi Tsuda, taught there as an assistant professor and professor, and served as president of Taisho University.
